paragraphs.text: Expose the running DeepSeek Harness desktop web GUI to a phone - the same session through a loopback
reverse proxy, with LAN and Tailscale token URLs. No second harness.
# dsh-lan-remote
Expose the running DeepSeek Harness web GUI to your LAN so a phone can drive **the same** session (n
ot a second harness instance). With Tailscale on both machines it also works when the phone is on an
rness instance). With Tailscale on both machines it also works when the phone is on another network.
English | 中文
The desktop build binds its web server to `127.0.0.1` and rejects wildcard addresses such as `0.0.0.
0`. This plugin leaves that binding alone and starts a reverse proxy on `0.0.0.0:<port>` that forwar
ds to the host's loopback port, so the phone talks to the instance the desktop app is already using.
## Features
- Reverse proxy: LAN port → `127.0.0.1:<webServer.port>`, rewriting `Host` / `Origin` / `Referer` to

pass the host's auth fence (WebSocket upgrades forwarded too).
- Two URLs: the card shows both the
LAN URL (same Wi-Fi) and the Tailscale URL (any network), each with its own copy button. The remote

URL appears as soon as this machine is signed in to Tailscale.
- Floating handset button: bottom-rig
ht of the page, draggable, remembers its position; opens a card showing the current URL, a copy butt

on and a re-detect action.
- Announcements: on start it writes a desktop file and shows a toast; ema

il is optional (manual button or automatic on start).
- Mail settings: fill in your own SMTP server,
port, account, app password and recipient from the card. Stored under the plugin's `data/` director

y (password encrypted with Windows DPAPI). **No preset account ships with the plugin.**
- Status end
points: `GET /dsh-lan-remote/api/status`, `GET/POST /dsh-lan-remote/api/mail`, `POST /dsh-lan-remote
/api/mail/config`, `POST /dsh-lan-remote/api/restart`.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`dsh plugin add` writes it into the profile's `dependencies` and `dsh.profile.bundles`, so it starts
with the harness after a reload; `dsh plugin remove` unregisters it. You can also link the director
y into `<profile>/node_modules/` and register it yourself.
If the install hangs at `Progress: resolved ... added 0`, `<profile>/node_modules/` most likely stil
l holds an old link under the same name (for instance from an earlier `file:` install). pnpm has to
replace that directory, and on Windows a link that is in use makes it retry forever. Disable the plu
gin, delete `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-lan-remote` and `<profile>/node_modules/.ignored/*_tmp_*`, t
hen run the command again — it normally finishes in a few seconds.
## Configuration

## Remote access (Tailscale)
The proxy listens on `0.0.0.0`, so any address on any local interface works. Tailscale provides a wa
y to reach it from another network without a public IP or a tunnel service:

1. Install Tailscale on both the computer and the phone, signed in to **the same account**.
2. On th
e computer, `tailscale status` should show it online; note its `100.x.y.z` address (the plugin reads

it automatically — that's the "异地（Tailscale）" entry in the card).
3. Keep Tailscale connected on th
e phone and open the second URL.
Emails and the desktop file also list both addresses. If the card shows no remote URL, Tailscale isn
't running or signed in on this machine; after signing in, reopen the card or press re-detect.
## Notes
- The `?token=` in the URL is a credential equivalent to a login session; don't share or screenshot

it.
- Plain HTTP by default — use it on trusted networks or inside your Tailscale tailnet only; add

TLS or a tunnel for the public internet.
- The Tailscale URL sits behind the same auth fence: a bare

IP returns 401, so the full token URL is required.
- The phone needs the full token URL once; the b

rowser then keeps a 30-day session.
- After sleep or a network switch, press the re-detect button to
refresh the address.
